lessons.title: Keeper and centre-backs
lessons.objective: You can explain what a goalkeeper and centre-back do.

payload.prompt: Match the defensive role to its job.

pairs.definition: The only player allowed to use hands inside the penalty area; catches, punches and organises the defence.
A central defender who marks strikers, wins headers and organises the defensive line.
Any player whose main job is to stop the other team from scoring.

explanation.summary: The goalkeeper is unique because of hands; centre-backs are the central defenders.
explanation.sayThisLine: The keeper has the hands, the centre-backs organise the shape.

payload.prompt: Tap where the keeper and centre-backs start on a 4-3-3.

diagram.alt: A full pitch showing starting positions in a 4-3-3 formation with goalkeeper in goal, two centre-backs in front of goal, and outfield players further up.

explanation.correct: Right. The keeper is in goal, and the two centre-backs form the central defensive line.
explanation.incorrect: In a back four, the keeper sits in goal and two centre-backs defend the centre, with full-backs out wide.

payload.prompt: What is a centre-back's main job in defence?

options.text: Mark the striker and win headers

explanation.correct: Right. Centre-backs mark the opposing strikers and are strong in the air.
explanation.incorrect: A centre-back's job is to mark opposing forwards, win headers and organise the defensive line in the middle of the pitch.
explanation.sayThisLine: A good centre-back wins the headers and keeps the striker quiet.

payload.prompt: A goalkeeper can use hands anywhere on the pitch. True or false?

scene.alt: A goalkeeper attempting to pick up the ball with both hands outside the penalty area.

explanation.correct: False. A keeper can only use hands inside their own penalty area. Outside it, they're like any other player.
explanation.incorrect: Goalkeepers can only use their hands within their penalty area. Outside it, using hands is a handball offence.
explanation.sayThisLine: The keeper can use hands in the box, not outside it.

statement.speaker: Maya
statement.text: The keeper had a monster game, three saves in one-on-ones.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: The keeper faced tough one-on-one situations

payload.translation: The goalkeeper made three excellent saves in one-on-one situations with the striker, which saved the team from conceding.

followUps.line: Do you have a good keeper?
Who was the striker he faced?

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If you don't know the team, ask which keeper stood out.

lessons.title: Full-backs and wing-backs
lessons.objective: You can explain the difference between a full-back and a wing-back.

payload.prompt: What is the main difference between a full-back and wing-back?

options.text: Full-back defends the wing; wing-back attacks it
Wing-back plays in a back three and covers the whole flank
Full-back only defends; wing-back always attacks

explanation.correct: Exactly. A wing-back is a wide player in a back-three system who plays both sides of the ball.
explanation.incorrect: A wing-back is used in a back-three formation and covers attacking and defending across the whole flank.
explanation.sayThisLine: In a back five the wing-backs do double the running.

payload.prompt: Tap where the full-backs line up in a 4-3-3 formation.

diagram.alt: A full pitch showing a 4-3-3 formation with goalkeeper, two centre-backs, two full-backs on the wings, three midfielders, and three attackers.

explanation.correct: Right. The full-backs sit out wide in a back four, one on each flank.
explanation.incorrect: Full-backs play out wide beside the centre-backs in a back-four defence.

payload.prompt: Match the wide defender to their job.

pairs.definition: A wide defender in a back four who defends the flank and often overlaps to attack.
A wide player in a back-three system who covers the whole flank, attacking and defending.
An attacking player on the wing who beats defenders and crosses or shoots.

explanation.summary: Full-backs are in a back four; wing-backs are in a back three and do more attacking.
explanation.sayThisLine: Full-back or wing-back depends on the formation.

payload.prompt: A full-back overlapping means running forward to support an attack. True or false?

scene.alt: A full-back running forward past the winger to receive the ball in a wide attacking position.

explanation.correct: True. Full-backs often overlap, running forward to give the winger an extra passing option.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, overlapping is when a full-back runs past the winger to attack down the flank.
explanation.sayThisLine: The full-back overlapped and the winger went inside.

statement.speaker: Maya
statement.text: Our right-back gets forward more than the winger.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: The full-back is attacking more than defending
The full-back is playing high on the pitch
The team's right side is strong in attack
The winger is not trying hard enough

payload.translation: Her team's right-back is constantly overlapping and running forward in attack, more than the winger, making the right side dangerous.

followUps.line: Does that make your defence exposed?
Is he a threat from set pieces?

payload.noFakeExpertNote: It's fine to ask if that's risky for defending.

payload.prompt: Match the midfielder number to their role.

pairs.definition: Sits in front of the defence to break up play and start attacks from deep.
Links defence and attack, covers lots of ground and does everything—defending, passing, running.
A creative player just behind the striker who unlocks defences with clever passes.

explanation.summary: The numbers show their roles: 6 is defensive, 8 is box-to-box, 10 is creative.
explanation.sayThisLine: We need a proper six, someone to screen the back line.

payload.prompt: Tap the positions of the defensive, central and attacking midfielders in a 4-3-3.

diagram.alt: A full pitch showing a 4-3-3 formation with a defensive midfielder, a central midfielder, an attacking midfielder, and other players in their positions.

explanation.correct: Right. The 6 sits deep, the 8 is box-to-box, and the 10 sits behind the striker.
explanation.incorrect: In a 4-3-3 the three midfielders line up: the 6 shields the defence, the 8 covers everything, and the 10 creates chances.

payload.prompt: What does the number 6 do in midfield?

options.text: Screens the defence and breaks up play

explanation.correct: Right. The 6 is the defensive midfielder who sits deep, protects the back line and starts attacks.
explanation.incorrect: The number 6 is a defensive midfielder who shields the defence and wins the ball back.
explanation.sayThisLine: He's a proper six, he just sits and sweeps.

payload.prompt: What is the number 10's main role?

explanation.correct: Exactly. The 10 is a creator who unlocks defences with passes and movement.
explanation.incorrect: The number 10 is an attacking midfielder who sits just behind the striker to create goals.
explanation.sayThisLine: He's our number ten, everything goes through him.

payload.prompt: A number 8 is a midfielder who defends and attacks equally. True or false?

scene.alt: A central midfielder making a tackle in their own half, then running forward to support the attack in the opponent's half.

explanation.correct: True. The number 8 is a box-to-box player who covers the whole pitch.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, the 8 defends in their own half and attacks in the opponent's, earning the name box-to-box.
explanation.sayThisLine: He's the engine, an eight who does everything.

statement.speaker: Maya
statement.text: He's the engine, an eight who does everything.

payload.question: What role is she describing?

options.text: A player who runs all game
A midfielder who drives the team

payload.translation: She's talking about a number 8, a central midfielder who is the heartbeat of the team, defending and attacking constantly.
payload.noFakeExpertNote: It's fine to ask if he's the team's leader in the middle.

lessons.title: Wingers and strikers
lessons.objective: You can explain how a winger and striker create goals.

payload.prompt: Match the attacking role to their job.

pairs.definition: A wide attacker who beats full-backs, crosses or cuts inside to shoot.
The main goalscorer who leads the line, finishes chances and holds up the ball.
A striker whose game is being in the right place for tap-ins and rebounds.

explanation.summary: Wingers create from the sides; strikers finish chances in the box.
explanation.sayThisLine: Their winger destroyed our full-back all night.

payload.prompt: What is a winger's main way to create a goal?

options.text: Cross or cut back into the box

explanation.correct: Right. Wingers beat defenders and then cross or cut the ball back for teammates to score.
explanation.incorrect: A winger's job is to create chances by crossing from the wing or cutting back into the box.
explanation.sayThisLine: The winger whipped it in and the striker headed it home.

payload.prompt: What does a striker (number 9) do?

explanation.correct: Exactly. A striker is a finisher who leads the line and scores goals.
explanation.incorrect: A striker's main job is to score goals by finishing chances in and around the penalty area.
explanation.sayThisLine: He's a proper nine, lives in the six-yard box.

statement.speaker: Maya
statement.text: He's a poacher, nothing fancy, just always there.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: He's good at tap-ins and rebounds

payload.translation: Her striker is a clinical finisher who specialises in being in the box at the right moment to tap in chances, rather than dribbling or shooting from range.

followUps.line: Does he score many from open play?

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Poachers are valued because they finish chances; it's a real compliment.

payload.prompt: A striker always stays high on the pitch waiting for chances. True or false?

scene.alt: A striker holding their position high near the opponent's goal, ready to receive a pass or finish a chance.

explanation.correct: True. A striker's job is to stay high and be ready to finish chances.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, a striker leads the line and stays in an advanced position ready to score.
explanation.sayThisLine: The striker stays high looking for a chance to run on to.

lessons.title: Modern role labels
lessons.objective: You can decode box-to-box, playmaker and false nine.

payload.prompt: Match the modern role to what it means.

pairs.definition: A midfielder who defends his own area and arrives late to attack the other, covering the whole pitch.
A player, often deep, who sets the tempo and finds the key pass to unlock defences.
A centre-forward who drops deep into midfield to drag defenders out and create space for others.

explanation.summary: Box-to-box is a midfielder's hustle; playmaker is an artist; false nine is a forward who plays like a midfielder.
explanation.sayThisLine: He plays as a false nine so he's always dropping in.

payload.prompt: What makes a midfielder 'box-to-box'?

options.text: He defends and attacks equally, covering lots of ground

explanation.correct: Right. A box-to-box midfielder covers the whole pitch—his own box and the opponent's.
explanation.incorrect: Box-to-box means the player covers the entire pitch, defending in his own area and attacking in the opponent's.
explanation.sayThisLine: He covered every blade of grass, a proper box-to-box player.

payload.prompt: What does a playmaker do?

options.text: Sets the tempo and finds key passes

explanation.correct: Exactly. A playmaker is the creative heart, controlling the game's rhythm and unlocking defences.
explanation.incorrect: A playmaker is a creative player who controls the tempo and orchestrates the team's attack.
explanation.sayThisLine: He's the metronome, the whole team plays through him.

statement.speaker: Maya
statement.text: He plays as a false nine so he's always dropping in.

payload.question: What is a false nine?

options.text: A striker who plays like a midfielder
A forward who drops deep to create
A midfielder playing as a striker
A player who creates space for others

payload.translation: A false nine is a centre-forward who leaves the box and plays deeper in midfield to drag defenders away and create chances for teammates.

followUps.line: Does that give you an extra midfielder?
followUps.why: Shows you understand the tactical idea.
Asks if he's also a scorer.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: False nines are a tactical invention; it's fine to say it's clever.

payload.prompt: Complete these modern roles.
payload.template: A {{role1}} sets the team's tempo, while a {{role2}} covers every blade of grass.

explanation.correct: Right. The playmaker is creative and controls rhythm; the box-to-box is the engine.
explanation.incorrect: A playmaker directs play; a box-to-box midfielder runs everywhere.

lessons.title: The sweeper-keeper
lessons.objective: You can explain why modern keepers play like outfield players.

payload.prompt: What is a sweeper-keeper?

options.text: A goalkeeper who stays on the goal line
A goalkeeper who plays far off his line, sweeping and passing with his feet
A goalkeeper who only uses his hands

explanation.correct: Right. A sweeper-keeper is a modern goalkeeper who plays like a tenth outfield player, sweeping up and passing.
explanation.incorrect: A sweeper-keeper is a goalkeeper who leaves the goal area frequently to clear through balls and start attacks, like an extra defender.
explanation.sayThisLine: Sweeper-keeper, he's basically an extra outfield player.

payload.prompt: A sweeper-keeper helps the team build from the back with passing. True or false?

scene.alt: A modern goalkeeper playing far from goal, receiving a back pass and passing sideways to a defender in a build-up move.

explanation.correct: True. A sweeper-keeper is part of the build-up, passing with feet instead of punting long.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, modern keepers play out from the back with their feet and start attacks like a defender.
explanation.sayThisLine: He uses his feet to build up from the back.

payload.prompt: Match the goalkeeper style to its description.

pairs.definition: Stays on or near the goal line, catches crosses and punts the ball long.
Plays far from goal, clears through balls with his feet and starts attacks with passing.
How a goalkeeper releases the ball: throwing, rolling, passing or kicking.

explanation.summary: Modern football demands keepers who can pass and think like outfield players.
explanation.sayThisLine: Distribution is huge now, the keeper has to be able to pass.

statement.speaker: Maya
statement.text: Sweeper-keeper, he's basically an extra outfield player.

payload.question: Why is that good for a team?

options.text: He can start attacks from deep
He sweeps up balls over the top
He gives the team a passing option
He never has to make saves

payload.translation: A modern keeper who plays like a sweeper is part of the team's attack, sweeping up through balls and helping with possession, not just stopping shots.

followUps.line: Is your keeper good with his feet?
followUps.why: Shows you know what matters now.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If you don't know, ask if he's involved in the build-up.

lessons.title: Numbers on the shirt
lessons.objective: You can guess a player's role from a shirt number.

payload.prompt: What does a player's shirt number tell you?

explanation.correct: Right. Shirt numbers hint at roles: 1 is the keeper, 2-5 defenders, 6-8 midfield, 10 creator, 9 striker.
explanation.incorrect: Traditional numbers reflect positions: low numbers are defenders, middle numbers are midfielders, 9 is the striker, 10 is the creator.
explanation.sayThisLine: He wears the 10 for a reason.

payload.prompt: Match the shirt number to the traditional position.

pairs.definition: Goalkeeper; the sole starter and keeper.
Defenders; left-back (3), centre-backs (4-5), right-back (2).
Midfielders; 6 is defensive, 8 is box-to-box.
Attacking midfielder or playmaker; the most creative player.
Striker; the main goalscorer and leader of the line.

explanation.summary: Numbers go from goalkeeper (1) through defenders (2-5), midfielders (6-8), to attackers (9-10).
explanation.sayThisLine: The number gives you a clue about what they do.

payload.prompt: Complete the shirt number guide.
payload.template: The number {{pos}} wears the {{num}}, and the striker is the {{striker}}.

explanation.correct: Right. The 10 is creative and runs the attack; the 9 finishes it.
explanation.incorrect: The playmaker wears the 10; the striker traditionally wears the 9.

payload.prompt: If a player wears the number 10, what role do they usually play?

explanation.correct: Exactly. The 10 is traditionally the playmaker, the most talented outfield player.
explanation.incorrect: The number 10 is worn by the team's most creative player, usually the attacking midfielder.
explanation.sayThisLine: The number 10 is the team's key player.

statement.speaker: Maya
statement.text: He wears the 10 for a reason.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: He's the team's key creative player
He's trusted to orchestrate the team

payload.translation: Her team's number 10 is given that prestigious number because he's a highly talented playmaker or attacking midfielder who controls the team's creativity.

followUps.line: Is he your most creative player?
followUps.why: Shows you know what the 10 means.

followUps.line: How many assists does he have?

payload.noFakeExpertNote: The number 10 is a big honour; it's usually given to the best player.
